DONE. `analysis.py` + the three deliverables are written, and every one of your three conditions is enforced as an assertion in the script (the run aborts rather than shipping a bad table). Modelling chain exactly as approved — no changes.

## What was built
`analysis.py` (735 lines) implements, per (row × stream): Vcmax(T)=vcmax25·fT(T)·n_factor·btran with the CLM/Noah-MP curve incl. high-T inhibition → hard min(Wc,Wj,We)−Rd (C4; C3 branch dormant behind the same switch) → explicit cs from rb drawdown → Ball-Berry gs (b0 never scaled) → rs=cf/gs → Ci, closed by a damped (ω=0.5) fixed point with bracket maintenance and bisection fallback, tol 1e-8 Pa, ≤200 it. Night (PAR≤0): A=−Rd, gs=b0 exactly, cs/Ci still closed through the chain.

## Condition 1 — convergence (the deliverable)
All 5 cases reach the **identical** coupled fixed point (spread exactly 0.0 in all three columns):

| case_01 | 19.219376 | 31.220744321 | 39.207919058 | 167.130023434 | 31 |

Re-evaluated residuals at the reported answers: |dr_cs|=|dr_ci|=0.0 Pa, |dr_rs|=0.0 s/m, |dr_gs|=0.0 (light); max fixed-point step 9.67e-09 Pa; binding limitation Wc for all cases. An unrelated solver (scipy `brentq`, xtol 1e-12) reproduces the row-12 root to 0.0e+00 Pa and all 120 lit (row,stream) roots to **6.4e-14 Pa**.
n_iterations convention (documented in the docstring): index k of the closure evaluation at which the tolerance is first met, counting the evaluation at the supplied ci_init_pa as k=1 ⇒ "closure evaluations from the given start" = updates+1; night = 1.

## Condition 2 — uniqueness, bracket, limitation attribution
Sign-change histogram `{1: 120}` (time series) and `{1: 5}` (cases) — exactly one root per lit solve, asserted. **Bracket widening beyond ca: 10 time-series solves + 1 case**, with two distinct reasons separated, which corrects my plan-stage expectation: cases = 1 (`ci_init>ca`, case_04 only — case_03 starts at 0.9·ca and needs no widening), while the 10 time-series widenings are **`root > ca` because A < 0** on the five near-zero-PAR rows × 2 streams. Binding limitation over lit rows: sun Wc 55 / Wj 5; shade Wc 40 / Wj 20. **Shade light-limited (Wj) fraction of lit hours = 0.333 (20/60)** — that is the dawn/dusk ramp of A_shade, i.e. the prescribed convention, not an artefact. We=Wc crossover confirmed at Ci = p_atm/4000 = **25.3313 Pa**; no lit row has Ci below it, so We never binds anywhere and A_sun sits on the capacity plateau Wc−Rd on 55/60 lit rows, with Wc ∈ [22.175, 42.628] → A_sun spans 21.84–41.99 µmol m⁻² s⁻¹ over lit hours ≥1 W m⁻² (only low outliers: the 5 flagged rows at −0.4943).

## Condition 3 — alignment/units
120 rows, 1:1 with forcing.csv with `time_hr` matched by exact array equality; headers exact for both CSVs; no NaN/inf anywhere including all 60 night rows; those 60 rows have gs == b0 = 0.04 exactly; night A = −Rd ∈ [−0.435979, −0.225496]; Ci > cs > ca holds on all 120 night leaf-streams; Ci < cs ≤ ca holds on all light rows **except** the 5 flagged near-zero-PAR rows (10 leaf-streams) where A<0 makes Ci>cs>ca physically. A self-audit re-reads the written CSV from disk and re-derives all four closure relations plus the hard-min identity: max errors 7.11e-15 (A, Ci, cs), 1.36e-12 s/m (rs), 8.3e-17 (gs) — all ≤1e-6. Re-run is byte-identical (deterministic).

## Flagged rows and by-design deviation
time_hr 18/42/66/90/114 (par = 2.195e-13 W m⁻²) run through the **light** branch per your literal PAR≤0 rule: A=−0.49426, Ci=66.509, gs=0.03498. The gs floor 1e-6 never bound (asserted). By design, night gs=b0 rather than Ball-Berry at A<0, so |gs − BB(A=−Rd)| = 4.43e-3 mol m⁻² s⁻¹ (11.1% of b0) on the 120 night rows — printed as a NOTE, not a failure. esat convention stated explicitly in the log for auditability: **CLM/Buck 611.21·exp((18.678−Tc/234.5)·Tc/(257.14+Tc)) Pa**, R=8.314.

## Two deviations you should know about
1. **This environment has no matplotlib and no network** (pip fails on DNS; the venv is Python 3.12 while system Pillow is built for 3.14). Rather than ship no figure, I made plotting dual-backend: matplotlib when importable (unchanged code path), else a bundled dependency-free numpy PNG writer with a 5×7 bitmap font. `results/diurnal.png` (1180×800, two panels: A and rs for sun+shade, all 120 h, 5 cycles, night shaded) decodes as valid PNG with all chunk CRCs valid; I verified its data→pixel mapping to **sub-pixel accuracy** (median ≤0.47 px) by pushing synthetic exact linear ramps through the identical `make_figure` code, and confirmed the real figure's curves sit within ~1 px median of the CSV-mapped positions.
2. I added `results/solver_diagnostics.csv` (per-row limitation, Ci/cs/gs/rs, residuals, widening reason) as extra evidence. Not required; delete if you want a clean `results/`.

Key scientific outcome: A_sun == A_shade on 105/120 rows because the linear J=alpha_q·APAR with no Jmax cap exceeds Vcmax above PAR≈216 W m⁻² — even the shaded column (PAR_shade ≤ 358.5) is capacity-limited at midday; the streams separate only at dawn/dusk (15 rows). Daytime rs_sun ranges 107–390 s/m driven entirely by VPD (gs 0.235–0.390), and Ci_sun bottoms at 31.2 Pa at solar noon.
